description: Batched blocked Householder QR for the n=512 B=640 cluster (shapes 3,7,9,10 ~70% of baseline, all per-matrix-serial cuSOLVER). Replace the serial loop with ONE genuinely batched kernel: factor 32-col panels in SMEM (one CTA per matrix), form the compact-WY T-factor, apply the trailing update (I-VTVt)A as cuBLAS strided-batched TF32 tensor-core GEMMs across the whole batch, emit (H,tau) directly. Backward-stable, one path for all conditioning.

CholeskyQR2 + Householder reconstruction (TSQR-HR) for the n=1024/2048/4096 large shapes. Orthogonalize all-GEMM: G=A^T A then Q=A R^-1 (TF32/FP16 tensor cores, FP32 accumulate), a 2nd CholeskyQR pass plus one Newton-Schulz polish for orthogonality; then pivot-free Modified-LU of (Q-S) to emit geqrf-exact (H=Y, tau=diag(T)) and R=S*R_chol. Raise Gram accumulation precision (3xTF32 or FP32) on the ill-conditioned nearrank/clustered batches; route truly rank-deficient matrices to geqrf.

Fused register/SMEM-resident Householder megakernel for the small launch-bound shapes (n=32 B=20, n=176 B=40, n=352 B=40): one CTA per matrix, the WHOLE unblocked Householder factorization (column norms, reflector form, rank-1 trailing updates) lives in one persistent kernel with the panel cached in SMEM/registers, zero per-column kernel-launch storm and zero host sync. Emit (H,tau) in place. Target the per-launch overhead that dominates these tiny-n shapes.

Triton-authored batched blocked QR targeting the n=512 and n=1024 clusters. Author the trailing-update GEMMs (V^T C, then C-=V W) as Triton tl.dot kernels on Blackwell tensor cores (TF32 input_precision, FP32 accumulate), with a Triton panel-factor kernel using SMEM-staged column reductions. Use a persistent grid-stride over (matrix, panel) work-items so one launch covers the batch. Compare Triton tl.dot trailing update vs cuBLAS strided-batched to find the faster engine.

Low-precision FP8/BF16 trailing-update QR for the large n=2048/4096 shapes where the factor tolerance is loosest (~5e-3 to 1e-2). Blocked Householder with the two rank-nb trailing GEMMs in FP8-e4m3-in / FP32-accumulate (or BF16) tensor cores via cuBLASLt, panel and T-factor kept in FP32. One FP32 residual-correction sweep at the end to land inside 20*n*eps. Exploit B200 FP8 (~4500 TFLOPS, 2x BF16) on the most FLOP-heavy shapes.

Persistent single-launch megakernel for the n=512 B=640 cluster using thread-block clusters + distributed shared memory. One cluster of 2-4 CTAs cooperatively factors each 512x512 matrix with the panel shared via DSMEM/TMA multicast, tcgen05 tensor-core trailing updates (10.0a PTX), warp specialization (producer warps load/convert, consumer warps MMA). Grid-stride persistent over the 640 matrices so the whole cluster shape launches once. Emit (H,tau) compact. Attack launch overhead AND occupancy together.

Fork the global-best blocked-Householder kernel (brief 0, FP32 cuBLAS trailing). Add per-matrix classify-on-convert: in the SAME pass that casts FP32->TF32/FP16 for the trailing GEMMs (already touches every element), accumulate a cheap per-matrix conditioning stat (column-norm dynamic-range max/min, near-zero-column count). Gather the well-conditioned majority onto fast single-pass TF32/FP16 tensor-core trailing updates and the ill-conditioned minority onto the accurate FP32 path, then scatter back. Uniform TF32 fails the ill-cond n=512 factor residual; per-matrix routing is the unlock for the n=512/1024 cluster (7/12 of geomean) and passes the invariance guard.

Extend the global-best batched-Householder kernel (brief 0, 7480us/17.5x) to n=2048 and n=4096 — the only two benchmark shapes still routed to torch.geqrf and now dominating the geomean. Use brief 0's CUSTOM batched panel kernel (NOT cuSOLVER geqr2) for the panel factorization, which breaks the 92%-of-time serial-cuSOLVER-panel wall that capped the prior low-precision attempt, plus large TF32/FP16 tensor-core trailing GEMMs (factor tolerance is loosest here, ~5e-3 at 2048, ~1e-2 at 4096). These are tiny-batch (B=8, B=2) single-large-matrix regimes, so saturate tensor cores on the wide trailing update.

COMBINE the fast panel kernel (brief 0 HEAD 3d0ba1469, 7470us — panel now ~63-83% of time, trailing GEMM FP32) with the per-matrix classify-on-convert TF32 routing (brief 6 cce8a74d). On the slow-panel parent, routing only bought 1.038x because the trailing GEMM was ~10%; on the fast-panel kernel the trailing update is a much larger fraction, so routing the well-conditioned majority onto 1xTF32 tensor-core trailing GEMMs (band/rowscale/mixed stay FP32) should multiply far more. Integrate brief 6's _classify_well one-pass abs classifier + well-first reorder + split GEMM + inverse-permute onto brief 0's batched panel + bmm trailing path.

Attack the panel-factor bottleneck (now ~63-83% of the global-best 7468us kernel, latency-bound at 0.72 waves/SM) with a COOPERATIVE MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panel: a communication-avoiding TSQR-style factorization where 2-4 CTAs (a thread-block cluster) split the tall panel by rows, each factors its row-block, then they combine the small R-blocks via a reduction tree, sharing partial reflectors through distributed shared memory / global scratch. This exposes the row-parallelism the current serial single-CTA panel starves on (the panel is tall: m up to 1024+ rows, cb=32-64 cols), raising occupancy past 1 wave/SM. Fork off the current best so the fast bmm trailing update and T-factor are inherited; keep n in {32,176,352,512,1024} on the custom path and everything else on geqrf.

COMBINE the current global-best kernel (brief 0 HEAD 90eeb8f8, 6407us, with the 2-level tensor-core inner panel for n<=1024 but still routing n=2048/4096 to torch.geqrf) with brief 7's n=2048 extension (c2211dc): brief 7 brought n=2048 B=8 to 21394us = 3.47x faster than geqrf by routing it through the custom one-CTA-per-matrix batched panel + TF32 tensor-core trailing GEMMs (panel concurrency breaks cuSOLVER's serial-over-batch wall; TF32 stays well inside the loose ~5e-3 factor budget at n=2048). Add n=2048 to the supported custom path on top of the current best (n=4096 B=2 stays on geqrf since with only 2 matrices batched concurrency caps at 2x and the custom panel lags geqrf there).

COMBINE the global-best kernel (brief 0 HEAD 90eeb8f8, 6407us) with brief 2's specialized fused tiny-n Householder megakernel (186ad6fec) for the launch-bound small shapes. Brief 2 got n=32 B=20 -> 32.8us (9.8x), n=176 B=40 -> 558us (39x), n=352 B=40 -> 6377us (8.0x) with a one-CTA-per-matrix unblocked-in-SMEM kernel (odd-padded LDA=n|1 to kill bank conflicts; these shapes are CTA-barrier-bound + SM-starved, compute <10%, so NOT tensor-core-bound). The current best routes n=176/352 through its large-n-oriented panel kernel; adopt brief 2's tiny-n megakernel for whichever of n in {32,176,352} it measures FASTER per-shape than the current best, keeping the best's n>=512 path unchanged. AVOID the substring 'stream' anywhere in submission.py incl. comments (leaderboard ban-scan matches it).

COMBINE the new global best (brief 10 HEAD 7f589ebe, 5706us — tensor-core inner panel + n=2048 batched-panel extension, but trailing GEMMs are still FP32) with brief 8's per-matrix classify-on-convert TF32 trailing routing (a1882a4e). Brief 8 proved the TF32 trailing GEMM saves ~1500us at n=512 and ~1080us at n=1024 vs FP32 SIMT, with the win unmasked by a CUSTOM warp-per-row classify_kernel (144us, not torch's 1473us abs/amax/amin reductions) routing well-conditioned matrices to TF32 and band/rowscale/mixed-ill to FP32 (ill MUST stay FP32; 2xTF32 band 25.2>20). Port that cheap classifier + TF32-well/FP32-ill trailing routing onto the current best's trailing GEMMs for n in {512,1024,2048}; keep the panel and n>=4096->geqrf unchanged. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Attack n=4096 B=2 — now the largest remaining geomean term (still routed to torch.geqrf ~52k us; all other shapes are fast). Brief 7 showed the BATCHED panel loses here because with only 2 matrices there is no batch concurrency. So optimize for a SINGLE large matrix instead: blocked Householder where each 4096x4096 matrix's trailing update (I-VT^TV^T)C is a LARGE TF32 tensor-core GEMM (loose ~1e-2 factor budget at n=4096 makes TF32, even FP16, comfortably safe), and the very tall 4096xNB panel is factored with row-parallelism across many CTAs / a thread-block cluster (the tall-panel cooperative technique from brief 9: split m rows across CTAs, cross-CTA reductions via DSMEM, cluster.sync). Add n=4096 to the custom path; keep all other n exactly as the parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE the current global best (brief 12 HEAD 100b70f6, 5340us — tensor-core panel + TF32-trailing routing + n=2048, but tiny shapes still on the slower large-n-oriented panel: n=32 ~90us, n=176 ~635us) with brief 11's tiny-n consolidation (131d8ada) which adopted brief 2's fused tiny-n megakernel for n=32 (90->33us, 2.75x) and n=176 (635->557us). These tiny-n wins are ORTHOGONAL to the n>=512 trailing/panel work (shapes 0,1 use the megakernel, not the trailing GEMM), so they stack cleanly. Route n=32 and n=176 to the tiny-n megakernel (T=384 for n=176) on top of the current best; keep n=352 and n>=512 exactly as the best handles them. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Cut the host-side glue + redundant memory traffic AROUND the n=512/1024 trailing update in the current best (5340us). Profiling shows the per-matrix classify->reorder(gather)->split-GEMM->inverse-permute(scatter) wrapper costs ~448us (4.7%) at n=512 just in the mixed reorder gather, plus per-panel host launches. FUSE it: (a) scatter-on-write so the trailing GEMM writes directly to the final permuted position (no separate inverse-permute gather), (b) replace the python per-panel loop driving cuBLAS bmm + classify with a single persistent driver / CUDA-graph capture so the ~N/NB panel steps issue without per-step host launch overhead, (c) avoid materializing the reordered copy of the whole batch. Keep the tensor-core panel and TF32/FP32 per-matrix routing semantics identical; this is purely killing the orchestration overhead and extra HBM passes. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Attack n=352 B=40 (~1612us) — the largest tiny/medium shape and NEITHER existing kernel's strength. The 352x352 FP32 matrix (495KB) overruns the single-CTA 227KB SMEM cap, so the fused whole-matrix megakernel can't apply and it currently runs the large-n-oriented blocked panel+cuBLAS path. Build a path that fits: either a 2-pass / panel-resident SMEM megakernel (only the active NB-wide panel + the WMMA trailing tiles live in SMEM; the trailing block is loaded incrementally from global, like the n=512/1024 fused megakernel does) processing one matrix per CTA, OR a multi-CTA-tiled cooperative factorization splitting the 352 rows across CTAs. Both make the 40-matrix batch (SM-rich) factor concurrently in one launch, killing the per-panel cuBLAS launch storm. Keep all other n exactly as parent. FP32 panel (TF32 panel fails the gate); avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Push the n=1024/2048 trailing-update GEMMs to FP8 (e4m3) or NVFP4 block-scaled tensor cores (B200 FP8 ~4500 TFLOPS = 2x TF32, NVFP4 ~9000 = 4x), with per-block absmax scaling and a CHEAP FP32 RE-ORTHOGONALIZATION correction to recover accuracy — the operator's specifically-requested lever. The current best routes well-conditioned trailing GEMMs to 1xTF32; FP8/FP4 doubles/quadruples that throughput. The factor budget is loose at n=1024 (~2.4e-3) and n=2048 (~5e-3). A prior attempt found naive FP8 _scaled_mm failed at low batch WITHOUT correction; the new idea is FP8/FP4 GEMM + one FP32 residual-correction pass (recompute the trailing block's high-order error in FP32 and add it back, or a single Newton-Schulz/Gram-Schmidt reorthogonalization of the affected columns). Per-matrix route: well-conditioned -> FP8/FP4+correction, ill -> existing FP32/TF32. Validate AND note remote-portability risk (BF16x9 passed local but failed remote — so any low-precision path must be confirmed remotely later). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE the global best (brief 14 HEAD 1fbce1e9, 4861us) with brief 0's latest fully-FP32-optimized 2-level panel (c915758fd): brief 0 drove its panel through a 2-level block-WY restructure, fused write-back+V-build, launch_bounds no-spill, coalesced HBM, taking the n=512 cluster to ~9.5k/shape (~10x over serial cuSOLVER). The best's n=512/1024 panel may predate these — n=512/1024 are 5 of 12 shapes (the geomean bulk), so any unintegrated panel speedup there moves the geomean most. Bring brief 0's latest panel_factor kernel onto the best, keeping the best's tiny-n megakernel, TF32 trailing routing, and n=2048 path. Re-measure with min-of-3 (benchmark is bimodal ~X/~2X). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Software-pipeline the blocked-QR loop to overlap panel-j+1 factorization with panel-j's trailing-update GEMM, which are currently SERIAL (panel ~50-77% of time, trailing GEMM ~27-48%, run back-to-back). The look-ahead / left-looking pipeline: while the cuBLAS TF32 trailing GEMM for the current panel runs, factor the NEXT panel's leading block on the just-updated columns concurrently, so the panel kernel's latency hides under the GEMM throughput. Apply across n=512/1024/2048. This attacks the serial host-side dependency chain (a distinct lever from making either kernel individually faster). Use CUDA graphs or careful kernel ordering on the default queue; do NOT write the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments (use synonyms; the ban-scan matches it). Keep correctness exact vs torch.geqrf; re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal benchmark).

COMBINE the current global best (brief 19 HEAD 7d87b96a, ~4860us, which still routes n=4096 to torch.geqrf ~52k us — the LARGEST remaining geomean term) with brief 13's n=4096 cooperative-cluster win (6dfdc0736): brief 13 got n=4096 B=2 to 31448us = 1.66x faster than geqrf via a thread-block cluster of K=16 CTAs (hardware cap) splitting one tall 4096-row panel by rows, cross-CTA reductions via DSMEM/cluster.sync (sm_100a), hybrid (cluster for tall panels m>=256, single-CTA for short), whole-batch TF32 trailing GEMM (loosest budget ~1.2e-2 at n=4096). This n=4096 path is ORTHOGONAL to the n<=2048/tiny-n/TF32-trailing wins in the best and stacks cleanly. Add n=4096 to the best's custom path via brief 13's _blocked_qr_cluster; keep everything else identical. Re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal benchmark). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE two confirmed orthogonal wins both near 4,585us from different lineages: brief 18's faster FP32 panel (361bc7a0, 4,583us — coalesced HBM load, zero register spill, fused write-back/V-build on the n=512/1024/2048 panel) AND brief 20's n=4096 cooperative-cluster path (8ae528bc2, 4,595us — n=4096 B=2 31k via K=16 thread-block cluster, was 52k geqrf). Brief 18 still routes n=4096 to geqrf; brief 20 has the OLD slower panel for n<=2048. Stack both: brief 18's panel for n<=2048 + brief 20's _blocked_qr_cluster for n=4096. The two diffs touch disjoint code (panel kernel vs the n=4096 routing branch) so they compose cleanly. Re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Speed up the n=4096 cooperative-cluster panel, now 66.7% of the n=4096 time (~31360us) and the largest single per-shape cost in the new best (250a694c, 4394us). The cluster panel_factor_cluster_kernel is single-level UNBLOCKED over its cb columns — it lacks the 2-LEVEL MICRO-PANEL (IB block-WY) restructure that the single-CTA n<=2048 panel already has (the FP32 restructure that cut that panel's serial-column-chain latency ~16%). Add the 2-level IB micro-panel inside the cluster kernel: factor cb in IB-wide sub-blocks, apply each sub-block's reflectors to the rest of the cb panel as a block-WY update, exposing parallelism the per-column cluster.sync chain starves on (profile shows it sync-bound at ~6.25% occupancy, K=16, 32 CTAs/148 SMs at B=2). FP32 panel (TF32 fails the gate). Also sweep more-rows/CTA at smaller K. Keep n<=2048 exactly as parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

BREAK THE PANEL WALL for the 900us goal: the FP32 Householder panel is 50-83% of EVERY shape and is the universal bottleneck (trailing GEMM is only 14-20% and memory-bound, two workers proved FP8 there is futile). Replace the panel's serial O(n^3) work with TENSOR-CORE GEMMs via per-matrix-routed CholeskyQR2 + Householder reconstruction: for WELL-CONDITIONED matrices (dense majority) compute G=A^T A and Q=A R^-1 on TF32/FP16 tensor cores (2 CholeskyQR passes for O(u) orthogonality; budget admits it at n>=1024 ~2.4e-3, n=2048 ~5e-3, n=4096 ~1e-2), then reconstruct geqrf-exact (H,tau) via the VERIFIED direct column-recurrence HR (recon err 3.8e-15, cheaper than no-pivot LU which capped the earlier FP32-only attempt). Route ILL-conditioned (band/rowscale/nearrank/rankdef/clustered) matrices to the parent's existing FP32 Householder panel. Integrate onto the current best (250a694c); start at n=1024/2048 (loosest budget, biggest panels) and extend to n=512 if accuracy holds. Reconstruction stays FP32. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE the current best (brief 21 HEAD 250a694c, 4394us — has the n=4096 cluster path but runs n=2048 B=8 on the SINGLE-CTA panel) with brief 20's n=2048->cluster routing (8f4c188f): brief 20 measured n=2048 B=8 goes 19197us (single-CTA, only 8 CTAs on 148 SMs = work-starved) -> 15240us = 1.26x by routing it onto the cooperative cluster panel with K=8 (lower K at higher batch — the K-by-batch law: n=4096 B=2 wants K=16, n=2048 B=8 wants K=8). Add the n=2048->cluster routing branch onto the best (which already has the cluster kernel for n=4096). Keep n=4096 cluster (K=16) and everything else exactly as the best. Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

COMBINE the current best (brief 21 HEAD 250a694c, 4394us) with brief 16's n=352 tuning win (01c41008): brief 16 cut n=352 B=40 from 1617us to 1529us (~5.3% shape, ~0.5% geomean) by widening the n=352 blocked-panel cb 16->32 (halves 22->11 panel/trailing launches) and panel CTA threads 128->256 (shortens the tall per-column reductions). Apply brief 16's n=352 parameters onto the best; keep all other n exactly as the best. FP32. Re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Attack the n=512 B=640 cluster (4 of 12 shapes, ~7.8k us each = the largest absolute geomean cost), the one SM-SATURATED regime (640 matrices >> 148 SMs, so compute/panel-bound, NOT latency-bound like n=2048/4096). A sibling found panel-vs-trailing OVERLAP wins ~13% but only via a BANNED non-default CUDA queue; the REMOTE-SAFE version is a FUSED SINGLE-KERNEL look-ahead: factor panel j+1's leading block and run panel j's wide trailing update inside ONE persistent kernel on the default queue (no extra queue), so the panel latency hides under the trailing GEMM via warp specialization / async SMEM pipelining (cp.async) rather than cross-queue concurrency. One CTA per matrix at B=640 fills the GPU. FP32 panel (TF32 fails the gate); per-matrix TF32/FP32 trailing as in parent. Keep all other n exactly as parent (b050aa33). Single default queue only — do NOT use a non-default CUDA queue and do NOT write or obfuscate the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Kill the host-device SYNC and the reorder COPY in the n=512/1024 trailing update with a DEVICE-SIDE per-matrix-routed trailing epilogue. A sibling measured the current path pays: a classify->.item() route that DRAINS the pipeline (host reads n_well to pick GEMM batch counts) plus a mandatory ~208us input copy + mixed reorder gather (~433us, HBM-bound) because cuBLAS factors out-of-place and needs the well-conditioned matrices gathered contiguous. Replace it: run the trailing update as a single custom batched kernel that, per matrix, applies V T^T V^T C in TF32 (well) or FP32 (ill) using the per-matrix class flag IN-KERNEL (no host n_well, no gather/scatter, no .item() sync) — write results in place. This removes the host sync AND the reorder copy at once (the sibling's open direction). Remote-safe: default stream only, NO non-default CUDA queue, do NOT write or obfuscate the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments. FP32 panel unchanged; keep n!=512/1024 as parent (b050aa33). Validate all 22 tests + 3 guards.

COMBINE the current best (brief 24 HEAD b050aa33, 4358us — has n=2048->cluster-K=8 routing) with brief 25's n=352 tuning (dc3a016e): brief 25 cut n=352 1617->1424us (-12%) by a 256-thread dispatch tier launching panel_factor_kernel<256> with cb=32 (constants _NB_352=32, _PANEL_THREADS_352=256). It's a 28-insertion/5-deletion orthogonal diff on the separate n=352 blocked-panel path, byte-identical elsewhere — but brief 25 forked the OLD best (250a694c) so its win isn't in the current best (which added n=2048-routing after). Apply brief 25's 28-line n=352 delta onto b050aa33; keep n=2048 cluster routing and all else exactly as the current best. Expected ~4358 -> ~4330us. FP32, no 'stream' substring. Re-measure min-of-3 (bimodal/contended — verify n=512 sentinel ~8.7k looks clean).

TSQR (communication-avoiding Householder) row-block panel for n=2048/4096 to break the cluster.sync WALL. Two siblings established: the cooperative-cluster panel is hard-walled (K=16 hardware cap, 6.25% occupancy, latency-bound on a per-column cross-CTA cluster.sync that CANNOT be removed — replacing it hangs). TSQR is the only structure past it: split the tall m-panel into independent ROW-BLOCKS, each CTA factors its block's QR with ZERO cross-CTA sync, then combine the small R-blocks pairwise up a reduction tree (log(#blocks) syncs total, not per-column). Reconstruct geqrf-exact (H,tau) via the worker-13-VERIFIED direct column-recurrence HR (recon err 3.8e-15). Big advantage over CholeskyQR (brief 23): TSQR-HR is backward-stable for ALL conditioning (exact Householder) so it needs NO per-matrix routing and handles the ill-conditioned n=2048 rankdef / n=4096 shapes natively. All-GEMM trailing on tensor cores (loose budget ~5e-3/1e-2). FP32 reconstruction. Keep n<=1024 as parent (b050aa33). Avoid the substring 'stream' anywhere incl. comments.

Route n=1024 B=60 onto the cooperative cluster panel — it is WORK-STARVED on the single-CTA path (only 60 matrices = 60 CTAs on 148 SMs), exactly like n=2048 B=8 was before brief 24 routed it to the cluster for a 1.26x shape win. The K-by-batch law: n=4096 B=2->K=16, n=2048 B=8->K=8, so n=1024 B=60 wants a SMALL K (2-4) — fewer CTAs/matrix, more matrices resident. Add n=1024 to the cluster-routed set with a swept small K; the cluster panel is FP32 Householder (stable all conditioning) and the trailing is TF32 (budget ~2.4e-3, safe). This is the same proven mechanism that won n=2048; n=1024 is 3 of 12 shapes (n=1024 dense/mixed/nearrank). Keep n=512/tiny-n/n=352/n=2048/n=4096 exactly as parent (b050aa33). NOTE: FP32 GEMM on B200 is SIMT not tensor-core, so the win here is OCCUPANCY/parallelism (filling idle SMs), not precision. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments.

Widen the single-CTA panel block width nb beyond 32 on n=512/1024 to cut the panel-loop iteration count (n/nb panels, each = a panel kernel launch + a trailing GEMM). The panel kernel's SMEM buffers (red[MAXCB*16], wsh[MAXCB], the cb-wide T-factor) HARD-CAP cb at 32 — raise MAXCB to 48/64, restructure those SMEM buffers (or move T to a padded SMEM tile), and sweep nb in {32,48,64}. Fewer/wider panels = fewer trailing-GEMM launches and fewer panel-kernel launches (the panel is ~50-60% of n=512 time and launch/latency-sensitive). The 2-level IB micro-panel already makes wide cb viable WITHOUT the quadratic serial-trailing blowup (a sibling measured cb=32 2-level is 2.3x faster than cb=32 single-level), so wider nb should now pay. FP32 panel. Keep n!=512/1024 as parent (b050aa33). Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments.

n=176 B=40 still runs the fused tiny-n megakernel / default 128-thread path and is launch/overhead-bound (a sibling found the same regime at n=352 and won −12% via a 256-thread/cb=32 panel tier). Now that the 256-thread panel_factor_kernel<256> template is instantiated and proven cheap (brief 28), test routing n=176 through the wider blocked panel (256 threads, cb=32) instead of its current tiny-n megakernel OR retune the megakernel's thread count — whichever is faster per-shape. n=176 is launch-bound (40 matrices, GPU mostly idle) so the win is fewer/cheaper launches. Measure n=176 (shape 1, ~557us) directly. Keep n!=176 EXACTLY as parent (d360cf57 = the de-facto best with the n=352 win). FP32. NOTE: FP32 GEMM is SIMT on B200 so this is launch-overhead not precision. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments.

Replace the per-panel cuBLAS strided-batched trailing GEMMs (n=512/1024, ~30-48% of time) with CUTLASS GROUPED/batched GEMM to cut the per-panel host launch count. Currently each of the n/nb panels issues separate torch.bmm calls (W=V^T C; C-=V T^T W) plus the per-matrix TF32/FP32 split — many small launches. CUTLASS grouped GEMM (KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized, sm_100, GemmUniversalMode::kGrouped) does variable-per-group GEMMs in ONE launch across the whole batch, and supports per-group precision so the well(TF32)/ill(FP32) split can be expressed without a host gather/reorder. This is a library-substitution distinct from removing the host classify sync; it attacks the trailing GEMM launch overhead directly. Build against stock CUTLASS bundled with torch if available, else a custom batched-GEMM kernel that fuses the two trailing GEMMs + the V/T apply into one launch per panel. Keep panel FP32, n!=512/1024 as parent. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments (CUTLASS warp-specialized is fine; just no non-default CUDA queue and no 'stream' text).

PERSISTENT BATCH-WIDE WORK-QUEUE megakernel — a distinct parallelization shape (the opposite of the current per-matrix-CTA approach) attacking the universal OCCUPANCY STARVATION. Every shape that bottlenecks is occupancy-starved at low GPU util (n=176 0.27 waves/SM, n=352 0.07, n=512/1024 work-starved) because one CTA (or cluster) is pinned per matrix and idle SMs can't help. Instead: launch ONE persistent grid of ~148*k CTAs that pull (matrix, panel-step) work-items from a global atomic queue, so when one matrix's panel chain stalls on its serial barrier, the SM steals the next available panel from ANOTHER matrix — filling the idle SMs across the whole batch. Blocked Householder, FP32 panel, TF32 trailing. The cross-matrix work-stealing decouples occupancy from matrix-count. Start with the n=512 B=640 and n=1024 B=60 shapes (most matrices to steal across). This is a from-baseline structural departure (082919481) for search diversity. HYBRID trailing update that removes the host sync + reorder WITHOUT replacing cuBLAS (which beats custom GEMM 3x — briefs 5/26/27). Currently n=512/1024 classify -> host n_well.item() -> gather well matrices contiguous -> 2 cuBLAS GEMMs (TF32 well group, FP32 ill group) -> inverse-permute. Instead: run the trailing GEMM (W=V^T C; C-=V T^T W) in TF32 over the WHOLE batch in ONE cuBLAS strided-batched call (no gather, no host n_well) — this is correct for the well-conditioned majority; THEN a small device kernel re-does ONLY the ill matrices (band/rowscale/mixed-ill, flagged by the existing device classify) in FP32 in place (recompute their trailing block at FP32 and overwrite). Ill matrices are the minority so the FP32 correction is cheap, and the bulk stays on fast cuBLAS TF32. Removes the ~448us reorder gather + the per-panel host .item() sync (the real overhead) while keeping cuBLAS GEMM throughput. Reuse brief-27's device per-matrix-flag infra. WIDE-nb panel at n=4096 with TF32 trailing — the one regime where widening nb PAYS. Cut the n=512/1024 trailing update from 3 cuBLAS bmm launches per panel to 2 by fusing the final subtract into a GEMM epilogue. Per panel the trailing update does W=V^T C (bmm1), W=T^T W (bmm2 or trmm), C -= V W (bmm3). The GEMMs are individually optimal (cuBLAS, confirmed unbeatable) — but each is a separate launch, and the panel loop runs n/nb of them. Fuse C -= V W into bmm3 via torch.baddbmm(C, V, W, beta=1, alpha=-1) so the subtract is the GEMM epilogue (already likely done — verify), AND fold the T^T W (bmm2) into bmm1 or bmm3 where possible: e.g. precompute V·T once (or T^T into the first contraction) so the three contractions become two. This is launch-overhead/orchestration reduction, NOT replacing the GEMM kernel (custom GEMM loses, 5× confirmed). Also try issuing the W=V^T C and the next panel's independent work so the scheduler overlaps them on the DEFAULT queue (no extra stream). Measure with nsys total-GPU-time + back-to-back A/B. FP32 panel; keep n!=512/1024 as parent; no 'stream' substring incl. comments.
